"""Create a new Pandas MultiIndex from the product of 1-d variables (levels) along a
        new dimension.

        Level variables must have a dimension distinct from each other.

        Keeps levels the same (doesn't refactorize them) so that it gives back the original
        labels after a stack/unstack roundtrip.

        """
        _check_dim_compat(variables, all_dims="different")

        level_indexes = [safe_cast_to_index(var) for var in variables.values()]
        for name, idx in zip(variables, level_indexes):
            if isinstance(idx, pd.MultiIndex):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"cannot create a multi-index along stacked dimension {dim!r} "
                    f"from variable {name!r} that wraps a multi-index"
                )

        split_labels, levels = zip(*[lev.factorize() for lev in level_indexes])
        labels_mesh = np.meshgrid(*split_labels, indexing="ij")
        labels = [x.ravel() for x in labels_mesh]

        index = pd.MultiIndex(levels, labels, sortorder=0, names=variables.keys())
        level_coords_dtype = {k: var.dtype for k, var in variables.items()}

        return cls(index, dim, level_coords_dtype=level_coords_dtype)

    def unstack(self) -> tuple[dict[Hashable, Index], pd.MultiIndex]:
        clean_index = remove_unused_levels_categories(self.index)

        new_indexes: dict[Hashable, Index] = {}
        for name, lev in zip(clean_index.names, clean_index.levels):
            idx = PandasIndex(
                lev.copy(), name, coord_dtype=self.level_coords_dtype[name]
            )
            new_indexes[name] = idx

        return new_indexes, clean_index

    def from_variables_maybe_expand(
        cls,

        variables: Mapping[Any, Variable],

        """Create a new multi-index maybe by expanding an existing one with
        new variables as index levels.

        The index and its corresponding coordinates may be created along a new dimension.
        """
        names: list[Hashable] = []
        codes: list[list[int]] = []
        levels: list[list[int]] = []
        level_variables: dict[Any, Variable] = {}

        _check_dim_compat({**current_variables, **variables})

        if len(current_variables) > 1:
            # expand from an existing multi-index
            data = cast(
                PandasMultiIndexingAdapter, next(iter(current_variables.values()))._data
            )
            current_index = data.array
            names.extend(current_index.names)
            codes.extend(current_index.codes)
            levels.extend(current_index.levels)
            for name in current_index.names:
                level_variables[name] = current_variables[name]

        elif len(current_variables) == 1:
            # expand from one 1D variable (no multi-index): convert it to an index level
            var = next(iter(current_variables.values()))
            new_var_name = f"{dim}_level_0"
            names.append(new_var_name)
            cat = pd.Categorical(var.values, ordered=True)
            codes.append(cat.codes)
            levels.append(cat.categories)
            level_variables[new_var_name] = var

        for name, var in variables.items():
            names.append(name)
            cat = pd.Categorical(var.values, ordered=True)
            codes.append(cat.codes)
            levels.append(cat.categories)
            level_variables[name] = var

        index = pd.MultiIndex(levels, codes, names=names)
        level_coords_dtype = {k: var.dtype for k, var in level_variables.items()}
        obj = cls(index, dim, level_coords_dtype=level_coords_dtype)
        index_vars = obj.create_variables(level_variables)

result.message:
Deliver patch-1: fix stack() upcasting int32 coordinate level to int64.

Root cause: PandasMultiIndexingAdapter.__array__ returned
array.get_level_values(level).values directly and ignored the dtype stored on
the adapter, so the original level dtype captured by PandasMultiIndex
(level_coords_dtype, set in create_variables) was dropped and pandas' i4->i8
upcast leaked into the stacked coordinate.

Fix (xarray/core/indexing.py): __array__ now defaults dtype to self.dtype and
materializes level values via np.asarray(..., dtype=dtype), preserving the
original index dtype for MultiIndex level variables.

Regression test added (test_dataset.py::TestDataset::test_stack_preserves_level_dtype)
covering the issue MVCE: Dataset(coords={'a': i4}).stack(b=('a',)) now has
i4 dtype for 'a'.

Verification on this exact version (v9): 216 focused public tests across
test_indexes.py/test_dataset.py/test_dataarray.py (stack/unstack/index/level/
MultiIndex), all passing, plus the new MVCE regression test passing.

result.message:
Deliver patch-2 (exact version v10): fix stack() upcasting int32 coordinate level to int64.

Behavior change (xarray/core/indexing.py): PandasMultiIndexingAdapter.__array__
previously returned array.get_level_values(level).values directly and ignored
the dtype stored on the adapter. PandasMultiIndex records each level's original
dtype (level_coords_dtype) and create_variables() passes it to the adapter, but
it was never applied when materializing level values, so pandas' i4 -> i8 upcast
leaked into the stacked coordinate. Now __array__ defaults dtype to self.dtype
and returns np.asarray(level_values, dtype=dtype), preserving the dtypes of the
indexes from which the MultiIndex is built.

Regression test (test_dataset.py::TestDataset::test_stack_preserves_level_dtype):
- literal issue MVCE: Dataset(coords={'a': i4}); ds['a'].values.dtype ==
  ds.stack(b=('a',))['a'].values.dtype, and result dtype is i4
- multiple levels with distinct narrow dtypes (i4, i2, object) preserved via stack
- unstack round trip keeps i4 / i2

Verification on this exact version (v10, public test sequence 51): the new
regression test passes and 226 focused public tests across test_dataset.py /
test_dataarray.py / test_indexes.py (stack/unstack/index/MultiIndex/level/dtype)
all pass with 0 failures.
